title: Computational phenotypes: traits, states, or moving targets?
description: At our September 25 meeting, we discussed individual differences, repeated measurement, parameter stability, and what makes a useful computational phenotype, drawing on Schurr et al. (2024) and the companion paper by Katahira, Oba & Toyama (2024).

title: What should EDM Megalab be?
description: Everyone in the Emory community with an interest in decision-making is welcome. Building on the broad participation at our September 25 meeting, we will get to know one another, map shared interests, methods, datasets, and opportunities, and shape priorities for the series. Join the conversation whether you attended last time or are new to EDM Megalab.

title: WIP presentations
description: Works-in-progress presentations from Pete Hitchcock on a decision-science approach to negative self-judgment in depression and Michael Hallquist on free-operant learning, vigor, and psychopathology, with time for discussion and feedback. presentations.title: Making Progress on Inherently Complex ("Low Essentiality") Disorders: A Case Study
presentations.description: Hitchcock introduces the idea that mental health problems vary in their inherent complexity and argues that depression and generalized anxiety are inherently complex, or low in essentiality. As a case study in making progress on these problems, he describes the lab’s decision-science approach to negative self-judgment in depression. This work builds on sequential-sampling models, in which decisions unfold by accumulating evidence over time: visual evidence for perceptual judgments, such as identifying a traffic light’s color, and personal value associations for food choices, such as choosing between Butterfingers and Reese’s.
